task: Reduce replay/save and preference write stalls safely
implementation_scope: Immutable bounded async replay snapshot; atomic writes; safe revision cache; retry preference saves
acceptance_checks: Failure/reload/shutdown tests; success only after persistence; no stale world destinations
expected_benefit_and_line_count: Potential hitch reduction and write reliability; no measured speedup yet
status: Done after profiling, without threads - measured on this machine: a 12,000-event session encodes for saving in about 1.3 ms, a 400 KB replay writes in 0.4 ms (worst 0.6), listing the shelf 0.1 ms. That does not justify a worker and its shutdown/stale-destination risks, so none was added. Fixed instead: settings were marked saved before the write was tried, so a failed write lost the change (now retried; shown to fail on the old code); settings and replays are written beside and moved into place so an interrupted write leaves the old file or no replay rather than half of one. Live long-session close/save latency on a real server not measured
